newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Oman envoy visits Jordanian inmates in Kuwait jail.
newsitem.headline: Oman envoy visits Jordanian inmates in Kuwait jail.

text.p: Oman's ambassador visited Jordanian prisoners in a Kuwaiti jail and said the inmates, said by their relatives to have been beaten by security men, told him they were treated well, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"They affirmed to me, during face-to-face interviews, that the treatment in the jail is excellent," Oman's Ambassador Nasser al-Kharousi told Arab Times after visiting 35 Jordanians in Kuwait's Central Prison.
In Amman, relatives had said that security men beat Jordanian inmates at the prison last month. The Central Prison has been rocked in recent months by unrest mainly among convicted drug smugglers.

Kharousi said the Jordanians were being kept in a special ward, away from prisoners held in criminal cases. "After the visit, we came to know that the whole issue (unrest) did not even involve the political prisoners."
Scores of Jordanians and Palestinians were jailed on charges of collaboration with Iraqi forces during the seven-month occupation of Kuwait in 1990-91.
Kuwait has denied the charges made in Jordan and invited the envoys of several countries in Kuwait to visit Jordanian prisoners.
Oman and Qatar accepted the invitation but the United States and Britain turned it down, the Arab Times reported. The British and U.S. embassies in Kuwait refused any comment on the issue.
Jordan has no embassy in Kuwait.

Kuwait's ties with Jordan were strained over Amman's sympathy for Iraq during the Gulf crisis. Kuwait says the time has not come yet to improve ties despite Jordan's move in mid-1995 to distance itself from Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
